title: The Coat With the Wrong Name
transcript:
I volunteered at the cloakroom during our town's winter concert. We gave each visitor a numbered ticket and attached the matching number to their coat. Most of the evening went smoothly, but after the performance a man returned a dark coat and said it was not his. The ticket number matched, and for a moment I thought he had simply forgotten what he had worn.

Then he showed me a name written inside the collar. It belonged to somebody else. I checked the nearby hangers and found another dark coat with almost the same number. When I had written the labels, one of my sevens looked like a one. Another volunteer had already handed that coat to a woman who had just left the cloakroom.

The concert organiser made an announcement in the entrance hall while I stayed with the man. Fortunately, the woman had stopped there to wait for a friend. She returned the coat, and both visitors checked their pockets before leaving with the correct items. Neither was angry, but I felt embarrassed about the confusion.

For the next event, we used printed number pairs instead of handwritten labels. We also separated the collection queue from the drop off area, giving volunteers more room to check tickets. I had originally blamed myself for being careless. Afterwards, I realised that changing a simple system could prevent the same mistake from happening to someone else.

questions.prompt: What proved that the first coat did not belong to the man?
options: It had a different colour from his ticket.
A button was missing from the sleeve.
The pockets contained a concert programme.
Someone else's name was written inside it.
questions.answer: Someone else's name was written inside it.
questions.explanation: 男士指出衣领内写着别人的名字，证明并非自己的外套。

questions.prompt: What had caused the coats to be confused?
options: A handwritten seven looked like a one.
A visitor had exchanged two tickets.
The printed labels had fallen off.
The concert organiser had moved all the hangers.
questions.answer: A handwritten seven looked like a one.
questions.explanation: 说话者手写的数字7看起来像1，导致同伴发错衣服。

questions.prompt: Why was the woman found quickly?
options: She had left her phone at the cloakroom.
She was still waiting for a friend in the entrance hall.
She had already called the concert organiser.
She returned to buy another concert ticket.
questions.answer: She was still waiting for a friend in the entrance hall.
questions.explanation: 她虽然离开了衣帽间，却还在入口大厅等朋友，因此听到了广播。

questions.prompt: What change was introduced for the next event?
options: Visitors were asked to keep their coats on.
Only one volunteer was allowed in the cloakroom.
Printed pairs of numbers replaced handwritten labels.
All coats of the same colour were refused.
questions.answer: Printed pairs of numbers replaced handwritten labels.
questions.explanation: 下次活动改用印刷好的成对号码，避免手写数字辨认错误。
